content: 1. The metabolism of tipranavir is influenced by the intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Grapefruit can increase the levels or effects of tipranavir by inhibiting this enzyme. Use caution and monitor closely when co-administering these substances. 2. Tipranavir reduces the effects of glimepiride, glipizide, glyburide, and other sulfonylureas through mechanisms related to insulin resistance. Reports indicate hyperglycemia due to insulin resistance with protease inhibitors. Use caution and monitor blood glucose levels in patients. 3. Tipranavir increases the levels or effects of guanfacine by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Strong or moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors significantly increase guanfacine plasma concentrations. For extended-release guanfacine, reduce the dose to half the recommended amount if co-administered. No specific recommendations are available for immediate-release guanfacine. 4. Tipranavir increases the levels or effects of haloperidol by inhibiting both CYP2D6 and CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor for potential adverse effects. 5. Tipranavir enhances the effects of heparin through pharmacodynamic synergy, which may increase bleeding risk due to its mild antiplatelet activity. Use caution and monitor for signs of bleeding. 6. Tipranavir increases the levels or effects of hydrocodone by inhibiting CYP2D6 and CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration with CYP3A4 inhibitors may lead to increased plasma concentrations of hydrocodone, potentially causing fatal respiratory depression. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 7. Hydrocortisone decreases the levels or effects of tipranavir by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor for reduced efficacy of tipranavir. 8. Tipranavir increases the levels or effects of hydromorphone by inhibiting CYP2D6 metabolism. Use caution and monitor for potential toxicity. 9. Tipranavir increases the toxicity of ibutilide by prolonging the QTc interval, raising the risk of QT prolongation and cardiac arrhythmias. Modify therapy, monitor closely, and consider alternative treatments if available. 10. Tipranavir decreases the levels or effects of ifosfamide by altering its metabolism through CYP3A4. This may reduce the formation of its active metabolite and increase toxicity. Modify therapy, monitor closely, and consider alternative treatments if available. 11. Tipranavir increases the levels or effects of iloperidone by inhibiting CYP2D6 metabolism. Iloperidone also increases tipranavir levels by inhibiting CYP3A4. Use caution and monitor for increased plasma drug levels. 12. Tipranavir increases the levels or effects of imipramine by inhibiting CYP2D6 metabolism. Use caution and monitor for potential adverse effects. 13. Indinavir increases the levels or effects of tipranavir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Both drugs increase the risk of immune reconstitution syndrome. Use caution and monitor closely. 14. Tipranavir reduces the effects of insulin aspart, insulin detemir, insulin glargine, insulin glulisine, inhaled insulin, insulin lispro, insulin NPH, and regular human insulin due to mechanisms related to insulin resistance. Protease inhibitors, including tipranavir, may cause new-onset diabetes mellitus, exacerbate existing diabetes, and induce hyperglycemia. Modify therapy and monitor blood glucose levels closely. 15. Tipranavir decreases the effects of linagliptin by affecting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporters and other mechanisms. Reports indicate hyperglycemia due to insulin resistance with protease inhibitors. Use caution and monitor closely. 16. Tipranavir decreases the effects of liraglutide through mechanisms related to insulin resistance. Use caution and monitor for hyperglycemia. 17. Tipranavir increases the levels or effects of lofepramine and lofexidine by inhibiting CYP2D6 metabolism. For lofexidine, monitor for symptoms of orthostasis and bradycardia, and consider dose reduction if co-administered with strong CYP2D6 inhibitors. 18. Tipranavir increases the levels of lumacaftor/ivacaftor by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. When initiating lumacaftor/ivacaftor in patients taking strong CYP3A4 inhibitors, reduce the dose to one tablet daily for the first week to allow for the steady-state induction effect of lumacaftor. No dose adjustment is required for moderate or weak CYP3A4 inhibitors. 19. Tipranavir increases the levels or effects of lumateperone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Reduce the dose to 5 mg/day if co-administered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 20. Lumefantrine decreases the levels or effects of tipranavir by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Conversely, tipranavir increases the levels or effects of lumefantrine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 21. Marijuana increases the levels or effects of tipranavir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 22. Tipranavir increases the levels or effects of mavorixafor by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporters. Monitor mavorixafor levels and reduce the dose if needed. 23. Tipranavir increases the levels or effects of medroxyprogesterone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy, monitor closely, and consider alternative treatments if available. 24. Tipranavir decreases the effects of metformin through mechanisms related to insulin resistance. Reports indicate hyperglycemia with protease inhibitors. Use caution and monitor blood glucose levels. 25. Tipranavir decreases methadone levels by increasing its metabolism but also increases methadone levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor for potential adverse effects. 26. Tipranavir increases the levels or effects of methamphetamine by inhibiting CYP2D6 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 27. Methylprednisolone decreases the levels or effects of tipranavir by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor for reduced efficacy of tipranavir. 28. Tipranavir increases the levels or effects of metoprolol by inhibiting CYP2D6 metabolism. Use caution and monitor for potential adverse effects. 29. Metronidazole increases the levels or effects of tipranavir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 30. Tipranavir increases the levels or effects of mexiletine by inhibiting CYP2D6 metabolism. Use caution and monitor for potential toxicity. 31. Miconazole vaginal increases the levels or effects of tipranavir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 32. Mifepristone increases the levels or effects of tipranavir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 33. Tipranavir decreases the effects of miglitol through mechanisms related to insulin resistance. Reports indicate hyperglycemia with protease inhibitors. Use caution and monitor blood glucose levels. 34. Tipranavir and mipomersen both increase the risk of hepatotoxicity. Monitor liver function tests (LFTs) closely when co-administered. 35. Tipranavir increases the levels or effects of mirtazapine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor for potential adverse effects. 36. Mitotane decreases the levels of tipranavir by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Mitotane is a strong inducer of CYP3A4; monitor for possible dosage adjustments when co-administered with CYP3A4 substrates. 37. Tipranavir increases the levels or effects of morphine by inhibiting CYP2D6 metabolism. Use caution and monitor for potential toxicity. 38. Nafcillin decreases the levels or effects of tipranavir by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor for reduced efficacy of tipranavir. 39. Tipranavir increases the levels of naldemedine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor for potential adverse effects if co-administered with strong or moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors. 40. Tipranavir decreases the effects of nateglinide through mechanisms related to insulin resistance. Reports indicate hyperglycemia with protease inhibitors. Use caution and monitor blood glucose levels.
